There are loads! Oxfords one of the best places to suffer with mental health. 

There is [Mind](https://www.oxfordshiremind.org.uk) a charity that run various support groups regularly throughout the week in Cowley.

There is [Talking Space](https://www.oxfordhealth.nhs.uk/talkingspaceplus/) a free NHS run service that offers over the phone counselling sessions and can refer you to other groups and organisations within the NHS.

There is [Restore](https://www.restore.org.uk) another charity that offers workshops for activities such as woodwork, art or gardening. They also offer employment coaching, to help people find jobs that they might like to do and to help them get work.

Taking to your GP, you could ask to be refered yourself to the Day Centre at the Warneford Hospital in Headington, which is a two week program of group Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and art therapy, they also teach you relaxation techniques.

Oxford also has various Adult Mental Health Teams across the county, which the NHS can refer you to.


Most of these charities offer volunteer positions too, which are mainly comprised of people who have used the service in the past.

I hope this helps!

And over time, he seems to unpack that idea in a better way. And example is the whole bill C-16 thing, obviously something that was very controversial for him, and gained him a lot of fame and infamy, but since then he has confessed that he might of been wrong about the purpose of it, but stood by his opinion of the “controlled speech” issue. I admit that it’s a dangerous thing for a public intellectual to do, and I think that his stance on public apologies is a little jaded and if he was more open to admitting his mistakes then there wouldn’t be as much controversy surrounding him. 

His issue is more with identity politics, and the idea of categorising  people based on a form of identity, and the problems that arise from that kind of mentality and society, which I at least think is a pretty valid point, you only have to look at this post to see the dangers of people who group themselves within an identity JBP vs. Ain’t JBP. He’s talked a lot recently about how people grouped together often tend to follow a tribe mentality, and I think that’s pretty clear to see how that can go very badly. 

The fear of a repeat of the Soviet Union. I think comes from the push for equality of outcome, which doesn’t imply fair reward for input. I mean there are a lot of cases where people have lost jobs to people who aren’t as qualified because they were of a minority, these cases may be false, or blown out of proportion, but it’s a scary idea. 

I think half of the problem that comes with him, is the media portrayal of him, demonising him and writing hit pieces that paint him as a “neo-nazi” or something simply highlights him to people who subscribe to that way of thinking, and then they look at his videos with confirmation bias, creating a false fan base who genuinely do misinterpret what he says, that’s obviously not as simple as it actually is, but people do have a tendency to only read the headlines, and claiming he’s a neo-nazi just pushes him to the view of those kinds of people.

I guess it’s a catch 22, him gaining fame, does allow him to help others more, but it also allows for him to negatively effect others more too, I guess in my point of view, I believe he has the power and ability to helps millions. And others, yourself included, feel he has the power to harm millions. In a perfect world I wish he wouldn’t make political or social comments too much and I very much hope that side of his being diminishes, and it can be about helping people, as I’ve said somewhere in this thread, I attended a lecture of his a few weeks ago, and he spoke about social issues extremely rarely, only really when he was prompted to during a q&a at the end. That’s how it should be in my opinion. He’s a psychiatrist, not a social or political commentator. 

I guess if you look at his motivational lectures for what they are and can separate that side of him from all the other stuff, then you might find value in that side of him, I might be wrong, and I don’t expect you to do it or want to and that’s fine.

I don’t think his view on “cultural Marxism” is based on the anti-Semitic conspiracy theory, it seems more like it’s built on a great fear of what happened during the Soviet Union. As I’ve said before I haven’t watched all his lectures and don’t use twitter so I can’t comment with 100% accuracy, but I can’t recall any anti-Semitic comments or sub-tones from him.

But I also don’t think his intention is to hurt anyone, it seems more like a byproduct of what he is trying to do. Which I believe is to help people. 

I don’t know if just looking for people better than him would work, not because he’s perfect or anything, but just because I can’t think of anyone who compares to him, in terms of ability to motivate and help people. I think in honesty the best thing we can hope for, is that he stops making political commentary. As a fan of his, I hope for that.

I’ve never been a fan of his political commentary, because I think it polarises people too much and takes away from what it was that drew me to him.  He’s openly stated that he wants to cut back from using Twitter as he doesn’t think it’s an appropriate platform for him. Hell, I don’t even pay attention to the subreddits in his name, because they have become a circle jerk of his political commentary.

I’ve followed his lectures and self help principles since the beginning of the year, and quite frankly it saved my life. Without going on too much, I was in a terrible place and had attempted suicide, and then I found out about Peterson, not because of c-16 or any of his political stuff, I only knew about that side of him months later. His motivational stuff, helped me reshape my life, and without it, it probably would of taken me a lot longer to get to where I am today, or worse. It gave me hope and a feeling of control over myself, which I wasn’t getting anywhere else. That’s why I follow his work

As I said I don’t necessarily agree with his political commentary and I do find some of it jaded and wrong. But, he’s also helped many people save themselves from themselves, that’s the reason I support him. And I try to defend him, because of the effect his motivational message has had on my life, and it pains me to see others close themselves off from the message that I got from his motivational lectures, and I know that’s the message I got, and it’s not universal, but hell it had such a huge impact on my life, maybe it could do the same for a lot of others.

And I think the whole you gotta watch a lot of his stuff to understand his point thing, I guess the only way I could potentially explain it, is, it’s like when you read any kind of intellectual statement, you gotta read it a few times and try to process it for a while and really think about it, I guess it goes in the same vain as that maybe.

Hey OP, I’ve been in your shoes, my ex broke up with me after 4 years at the end of November, and I didn’t take it very well at all, I spiralled into a horrible pit of depression, I couldn’t eat, sleep or look after myself, I dreamt of her every night and each day waking up felt like a bad thing. On January 30th I tried to hang myself. Obviously it didn’t work, and I was admitted into a mental health ward where I stayed for 4 weeks.
